defaultCompareInstruction: Two things are being compared here. "The rubric" is the list of ideal attributes between the RUBRIC START and RUBRIC END markers you were given. "The proposal" is the material between the PROPOSAL START and PROPOSAL END markers you were given separately — the actual document under review. From this point on, always use exactly these two names, "the proposal" and "the rubric" — never call either one "the context," "the ideal," "the ideal attribute," or any other name.

For each attribute in the rubric, in order, apply this test using three categories: mark it "Matches" (or "Exceeds" if the proposal goes further than the rubric requires) only if the proposal explicitly and specifically describes the exact thing that attribute calls for — the specific action, mechanism, or location named in the attribute, not just a general topic or category it happens to belong to. Mark it "Falls short" only if the proposal specifically addresses that same exact thing, but incompletely, partially, or with some real gap or limitation. Mark it "Not addressed" if the proposal never actually addresses the specific thing the attribute describes — this covers both a proposal that is silent on the topic entirely, and a proposal that only discusses something sharing a broader theme, category, or general subject area with the attribute without ever addressing the specific action, mechanism, or location the attribute names.

For example, if an attribute asks specifically about coastal wetlands or dune systems buffering wind impacts, a proposal passage about a completely different nature-based program — say, an urban tree-canopy or native-species planting initiative — is NOT a match or a partial match just because both are broadly "nature-based solutions." That passage does not address wind buffering, coastal wetlands, or dune systems in any way; it is a different specific action under a shared general label, and should be marked "Not addressed." Sharing a broad theme or category with an attribute is never, by itself, enough for "Matches" or "Falls short" — only actually addressing the specific thing the attribute names qualifies, even partially.

Respond with exactly one line per attribute, in this exact form: "<attribute name>: <Matches, Falls short, Exceeds, or Not addressed> — <one-sentence reason describing what the proposal itself does or does not say>. Quote: \"<a short phrase copied word-for-word from the proposal, or the word none if there is nothing worth quoting>\" [<source file name>, chunk <chunk number>]". Copy the quoted wording exactly as it appears in the proposal — never paraphrase, summarize, or invent it — and copy the file name and chunk number exactly from the [Source: ...] tag directly above the text you quoted. If you marked an attribute "Not addressed," write Quote: none rather than inventing one.

The rubric is only the standard you are checking against — never say the rubric is "mentioned in" or "part of" the proposal, and never say an attribute is addressed "in the rubric"; only the proposal can match, fall short of, exceed, or fail to address an attribute.

Make this call once per attribute and move on immediately — do not re-examine, re-derive, or change your answer for an attribute once you have stated it. If you find yourself genuinely torn between two categories for the same attribute, always choose the more conservative one and continue without switching back and forth: between Matches and Exceeds, choose Matches; between Matches and Falls short, choose Falls short; between Falls short and Not addressed, choose Not addressed.

Do not repeat, restate, quote, or summarize any part of these instructions in your reply, and do not add any preamble, acknowledgment, or introduction before your answer — begin your response immediately with the line for the first attribute.

attributes.name: EH12 - Local Capacity Building - Supporting Local Governments
attributes.proposal: How will the development of municipal heat resilience plans be supported?

attributes.name: EH13 - Local Capacity Building - Supporting Local Governments
attributes.proposal: Will technical assistance and funding be provided for local heat mitigation projects?

attributes.name: EH14 - Local Capacity Building - Capacity building
attributes.proposal: How will local officials and emergency managers be trained to respond to extreme heat?

attributes.name: EH15 - Local Capacity Building - Community Outreach
attributes.proposal: How will the response of community-based organizations to extreme heat be supported?

attributes.name: EH16 - Local Capacity Building - Data
attributes.proposal: What data will be collected to assess and respond to extreme heat?

attributes.name: EH17 - Local Capacity Building - Community Outreach
attributes.proposal: How will the public be informed about extreme heat risk?

attributes.name: EH18 - Local Capacity Building - Legal and Regulatory Frameworks
attributes.proposal: How will zoning and land use regulations change in response to extreme heat risk?

attributes.name: EH19 - Disaster Response and Preparedness - Emergency Response
attributes.proposal: What heat emergency response measures does the plan include?

attributes.name: EH20 - Disaster Response and Preparedness - Emergency Identification
attributes.proposal: What early warning systems are in place for heat waves?

attributes.name: EH21 - Disaster Response and Preparedness - Emergency Response
attributes.proposal: Are cooling centers available and accessible?

attributes.name: EH22 - Disaster Response and Preparedness - Emergency Response
attributes.proposal: How will vulnerable populations be protected during extreme heat events?

attributes.name: EH23 - Adaptation Strategies & Long-Term Actions - Heat Reduction
attributes.proposal: What strategies will be used to reduce urban heat islands?

attributes.name: EH24 - Adaptation Strategies & Long-Term Actions - Heat Mitigation
attributes.proposal: What long-term cooling infrastructure investments will be made?

attributes.name: EH25 - Adaptation Strategies & Long-Term Actions - Heat Reduction
attributes.proposal: Which nature-based solutions are proposed?

attributes.name: EH26 - Adaptation Strategies & Long-Term Actions - System Adaptation
attributes.proposal: How does heat resilience integrate with decarbonization and electrification goals?

attributes.name: EH27 - Adaptation Strategies & Long-Term Actions - Heat Mitigation
attributes.proposal: What criticial facilities require backup power for heat events?

attributes.name: EH28 - Adaptation Strategies & Long-Term Actions - Heat Mitigation
attributes.proposal: What incentives will vulnerable communities receive for energy-efficient cooling?

attributes.name: EH29 - Equity & Environmental Justice - Distribution of Impacts
attributes.proposal: How does the plan address disproportionate heat exposure in low-income communities?

attributes.name: EH30 - Equity & Environmental Justice - Community Outreach
attributes.proposal: How are communities engaged in desgning heat resilience?

attributes.name: EH31 - Equity & Environmental Justice - Community Outreach
attributes.proposal: What barriers do vulnerable populations face during extreme heat events?

attributes.name: EH32 - Equity & Environmental Justice - System Adaptation
attributes.proposal: Will heat resilience investments contribute to gentrification?

attributes.name: EH33 - Equity & Environmental Justice - Community Outreach
attributes.proposal: What ways will heat response be communicated?

attributes.name: EH34 - Equity & Environmental Justice - Distribution of Impacts
attributes.proposal: Will environmental justice communities be prioritized for cooling investments?

attributes.name: EH35 - Accountability & Governance - Roles and Responsibilities
attributes.proposal: Which agencies are responsible for implementing the state’s extreme heat strategies?

attributes.name: EH36 - Accountability & Governance - Funding and financing
attributes.proposal: What are the funding sources and mechanisms for heat resilience investments?

attributes.name: EH37 - Accountability & Governance - Costs
attributes.proposal: How much will heat resilience actions cost?

attributes.name: EH38 - Accountability & Governance - Indicators
attributes.proposal: How will heat risk and resilience be measured in the long-term?

attributes.name: EH39 - Accountability & Governance - Transparency
attributes.proposal: How will heat risk and resilience be reported?

attributes.name: EH40 - Accountability & Governance - Coordination
attributes.proposal: How will state and local governments, community-based organizations, and utitlities coordinate their efforts during extreme heat events?

attributes.name: G1 - Participation - Access to Information
attributes.proposal: Can stakeholders easily and independently access key scientific analysis, technical documents and policy papers to inform their opinions about risks and responses?

attributes.name: G2 - Participation - Access to Information
attributes.proposal: Does such information relate to climate adaptation as a whole, or particular risks?

attributes.name: G3 - Participation - Access to Information
attributes.proposal: Is information made available in the appropriate languages and formats?

attributes.name: G4 - Participation - Access to Information
attributes.proposal: How is the information communicated to non-technical audiences?

attributes.name: G5 - Participation - Meaningful Opportunities
attributes.proposal: Are stakeholders provided with meaningful opportunities to participate in climate change preparation and adaption?

attributes.name: G6 - Participation - Meaningful Opportunities
attributes.proposal: What measures beyond traditional notice and comment period are provided?

attributes.name: G7 - Participation - Inclusiveness
attributes.proposal: Can you please provide examples where state plans identify populations in states of vulnerability (e.g., disabled, EJ populations, youth, immigrants, etc.) and facilitate their participation in policy-making?

attributes.name: G8 - Participation - On-going Involvement
attributes.proposal: Is the on-going involvement of key stakeholders encouraged (e.g., maintaining active dialogues, informing participations of the results and impact of their inputs, etc.)?

attributes.name: G9 - Institutions - Goal Definition
attributes.proposal: Is there a clear definition of what ‘climate resilience’ and ‘climate adaptation’ would mean in the state?

attributes.name: G10 - Institutions - Goal Definition
attributes.proposal: Are the policy measures to achieve that goal gathered in one plan that is periodically revised?

attributes.name: G11 - Institutions - Political Leadership
attributes.proposal: Is strong political leadership shaping and supporting climate adaptation policy?

attributes.name: G12 - Institutions - Political Leadership
attributes.proposal: Is the climate adaptation plan required by statue or an executive order?

attributes.name: G13 - Institutions - Technical Leadership
attributes.proposal: Is there a dedicated climate resilience officer at the highest level of state government?

attributes.name: G14 - Institutions - Technical Leadership
attributes.proposal: Is there an administrative office committed to climate adaptation?

attributes.name: G15 - Institutions - Technical Leadership
attributes.proposal: Are the roles and responsibilities of the office committed to cliamte adapatation defined in enabling legislation or state policy?

attributes.name: G16 - Institutions - Agency Cooperation
attributes.proposal: Are there strong mechanisms to ensure that government agencies are achieving the same climate adaptation ends in ways that increase efficiency through cooperation?

attributes.name: G17 - Institutions - Agency Cooperation
attributes.proposal: Is there an explicit understanding of how climate adaptation can be reflected in such departments priorities?

attributes.name: G18 - Institutions - Legal and Regulatory Framework
attributes.proposal: Are the governance arrangements for the climate adaptation plan supported by a framework of laws and executive orders?

attributes.name: G19 - Institutions - Expertise
attributes.proposal: Does the institutional framework encourage the use of best scientific evidence for risk identification and responsive policy design?

attributes.name: G20 - Institutions - Expertise
attributes.proposal: Is there a process for incorporating new findings as they emerge?

attributes.name: G21 - Institutions - Expertise
attributes.proposal: Does the plan mention consultation with expert bodies (e.g., climate scientists, engineers)?

attributes.name: G22 - Institutions - Expertise
attributes.proposal: Is there a formal advisory council of experts to guide the plan's development and evaluation?

attributes.name: G23 - Institutions - Expertise
attributes.proposal: Are mechanisms in place to allow for expert input during planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation?

attributes.name: G24 - Institutions - Capacity Development
attributes.proposal: Does the climate adaptation plan address increasing the capability of government departments and employees to identify and address risks arising from climate adaptation?

attributes.name: G25 - Transparency - Quality
attributes.proposal: Does the data provided give the public an on-going sense of the risks of climate adaptation and the progress of policy measures to prepare, respond to and recover from them?

attributes.name: G26 - Transparency - Quality
attributes.proposal: Is there a clear audit trail and verification mechanism?

attributes.name: G27 - Transparency - Granularity
attributes.proposal: Are the data and reports provided sufficiently granular to provide a clear picture at the community level, without masking outcomes or impacts on vulnerable populations?

attributes.name: G28 - Transparency - Granularity
attributes.proposal: Have clear, useful metrics been developed?

attributes.name: G29 - Transparency - Speed and Frequency
attributes.proposal: Is information provided sufficiently quickly and with enough frequency to give stakeholders a solid understanding of a climate adaptation risk or policy?

attributes.name: G30 - Transparency - Speed and Frequency
attributes.proposal: Are data and reports stale or irrelevant by the time the public has access?

attributes.name: G31 - Transparency - Reach
attributes.proposal: Is the information made available to all impacted stakeholders in a manner that facilitates their understanding?

attributes.name: G32 - Accountability - Clarity
attributes.proposal: Are roles, responsibilities and objectives clearly delineated?

attributes.name: G33 - Accountability - Enforceability
attributes.proposal: Do citizens have statutory rights to enforce the climate adaptation policy or pursue breaches?

attributes.name: G34 - Accountability - Enforceability
attributes.proposal: Does the plan outline the consequences for departments or entities that fail to meet their obligations?

attributes.name: G35 - Accountability - Systematic
attributes.proposal: Is there a systematic approach to monitoring, evaluation, publication and learning to maximize positive outcomes and learning?

attributes.name: G36 - Resources - Human Resources
attributes.proposal: Are enough people with a broad range of skills giving enough attention to the critical climate adaptation risks?

attributes.name: G37 - Resources - Human Resources
attributes.proposal: Does the plan invest in building the skills of state employees needed to address climate adaptation issues?

attributes.name: G38 - Resources - Public Financial Resources
attributes.proposal: Does the plan provide estimated costs of increasing the resilience of key physical and natural assets?  Are funding mechanisms identified to cover those costs?

attributes.name: G39 - Resources - Public Financial Resources
attributes.proposal: Is it identified and protected in state budgets?

attributes.name: G40 - Resources - Public Financial Resources
attributes.proposal: Does the plan provide dedicated funding for proactive climate adaptation measures, separate from funding for disaster recovery?

attributes.name: G41 - Resources - Private Financial Resources
attributes.proposal: Does the plan provide incentives that encourage private investment in climate resilience measures? Are the resources required from private investment quantified?

attributes.name: G42 - Resources - Private Financial Resources
attributes.proposal: Do these incentives advance or detract from efforts to ensure public climate readiness?

attributes.name: G43 - Resources - Access
attributes.proposal: Are financial, human and knowledge resources made available to regional/municipal entities?

attributes.name: Haz1 - Hazard Identification - Comprehensive Hazard Coverage
attributes.proposal: Has the plan identified all major natural hazards relevant to the municipality’s geography and climate conditions?

attributes.name: Haz2 - Hazard Identification - Locally Significant Hazards
attributes.proposal: Are locally significant hazards included even if they are not among the most severe statewide hazards?

attributes.name: Haz3 - Hazard Identification - Future Climate Conditions
attributes.proposal: Does the plan consider both current and future climate-driven changes in hazard frequency, intensity, duration, or geographic extent?

attributes.name: Haz4 - Hazard Identification - Compound and Cascading Hazards
attributes.proposal: Does the plan evaluate compound or cascading hazards, such as flooding combined with power outages, heat combined with poor air quality, or coastal flooding combined with storm surge?

attributes.name: Haz5 - Hazard Identification - Hazard Inclusion and Exclusion Rationale
attributes.proposal: Does the plan explain why certain hazards were included or excluded from analysis?

attributes.name: Haz6 - Asset Inventory and Exposure - Critical Asset Inventory
attributes.proposal: Has the plan identified and mapped critical facilities, infrastructure, natural resources, and community assets?

attributes.name: Haz7 - Asset Inventory and Exposure - Essential Community Facilities
attributes.proposal: Does the asset inventory include affordable housing, public housing, schools, childcare facilities, healthcare facilities, emergency response facilities, transportation infrastructure, water and wastewater infrastructure, energy infrastructure, and community cooling or warming centers?

attributes.name: Haz8 - Asset Inventory and Exposure - Assets Serving Priority Populations
attributes.proposal: Does the plan identify assets that serve Environmental Justice communities and low-income, older adult, disabled, immigrant, or linguistically isolated populations?

attributes.name: Haz9 - Asset Inventory and Exposure - Natural and Nature-Based Assets
attributes.proposal: Are natural and nature-based assets included, such as wetlands, floodplains, urban forests, coastal buffers, and open space?

attributes.name: Haz10 - Asset Inventory and Exposure - Criticality Assessment
attributes.proposal: Does the plan identify which assets are most critical to life safety, public health, and community functioning during and after disasters?

attributes.name: Haz11 - Asset Inventory and Exposure - Exposure Quantification
attributes.proposal: Does the plan quantify the number of people, buildings, facilities, and acres exposed to each hazard?

attributes.name: Haz12 - Data Quality and Data Sources - Source Documentation
attributes.proposal: Are the data sources used clearly documented and cited?

attributes.name: Haz13 - Data Quality and Data Sources - Data Currency
attributes.proposal: Were the most recent datasets available at the time of plan development used?

attributes.name: Haz14 - Data Quality and Data Sources - Best Available Local and State Data
attributes.proposal: Does the plan use state-specific or locally developed hazard datasets when available rather than relying exclusively on national datasets?

attributes.name: Haz15 - Data Quality and Data Sources - Flood Risk Data
attributes.proposal: For flooding analyses, does the plan incorporate the best available flood data, including state flood-risk tools, watershed studies, or local modeling where available?

attributes.name: Haz16 - Data Quality and Data Sources - Data Limitations and Uncertainty
attributes.proposal: Does the plan explain limitations and uncertainties associated with the data sources used?

attributes.name: Haz17 - Data Quality and Data Sources - Demographic Data Currency
attributes.proposal: Are demographic and socioeconomic datasets sufficiently current to reflect recent community conditions?

attributes.name: Haz18 - Data Quality and Data Sources - Historical and Projected Evidence
attributes.proposal: Are historical disaster records used alongside future climate projections?

attributes.name: Haz19 - Hazard Measurement and Modeling - Risk Measurement Method
attributes.proposal: Does the plan clearly explain how hazard risk was measured?

attributes.name: Haz20 - Hazard Measurement and Modeling - Model Assumptions
attributes.proposal: Are assumptions used in risk calculations transparently documented?

attributes.name: Haz21 - Hazard Measurement and Modeling - Risk Rating Method
attributes.proposal: Does the plan explain how hazard probability, severity, exposure, and vulnerability were combined to generate risk ratings?

attributes.name: Haz22 - Hazard Measurement and Modeling - Future Climate Projections
attributes.proposal: Does the plan use future climate projections when assessing long-term risk?

attributes.name: Haz23 - Hazard Measurement and Modeling - Planning Horizons
attributes.proposal: Are planning horizons clearly specified, such as current conditions, 2050, 2070, or 2100?

attributes.name: Haz24 - Hazard Measurement and Modeling - Technical Appropriateness
attributes.proposal: Are the methods used to model hazards technically appropriate and supported by scientific evidence?

attributes.name: Haz25 - Hazard Measurement and Modeling - Risk Concept Clarity
attributes.proposal: Does the plan distinguish among hazard exposure, vulnerability, and risk?

attributes.name: Haz26 - Hazard Measurement and Modeling - Projection Uncertainty
attributes.proposal: Are uncertainties in climate projections explicitly discussed?

attributes.name: Haz27 - Vulnerability Assessment - Population Vulnerability by Hazard
attributes.proposal: Does the plan evaluate which populations are most vulnerable to each hazard?

attributes.name: Haz28 - Vulnerability Assessment - Social Vulnerability Indicators
attributes.proposal: Does the assessment incorporate social vulnerability indicators such as income, age, disability status, race and ethnicity, language isolation, housing tenure, and health status?

attributes.name: Haz29 - Vulnerability Assessment - Cumulative Vulnerability
attributes.proposal: Does the plan identify neighborhoods experiencing multiple overlapping vulnerabilities?

attributes.name: Haz30 - Vulnerability Assessment - Spatial Analysis of Vulnerability
attributes.proposal: Does the plan map social vulnerability alongside hazard exposure?

attributes.name: Haz31 - Vulnerability Assessment - Displacement and Economic Risk
attributes.proposal: Does the plan consider the risk of displacement, housing instability, or economic disruption resulting from climate hazards?

attributes.name: Haz32 - Vulnerability Assessment - Public Health Impacts
attributes.proposal: Does the plan assess public health impacts associated with identified hazards?

attributes.name: Haz33 - Risk Prioritization - Transparent Prioritization Process
attributes.proposal: Does the plan provide a transparent process for prioritizing hazards?

attributes.name: Haz34 - Risk Prioritization - Prioritization Criteria
attributes.proposal: Are prioritization criteria clearly defined?

attributes.name: Haz35 - Risk Prioritization - Likelihood and Consequence
attributes.proposal: Are both likelihood and consequence considered in prioritization?

attributes.name: Haz36 - Risk Prioritization - Equity in Prioritization
attributes.proposal: Are impacts to vulnerable populations weighted or considered separately in prioritization methods?

attributes.name: Haz37 - Risk Prioritization - Highest-Risk People, Assets, and Systems
attributes.proposal: Does the plan identify which assets, populations, and systems face the highest overall risk?

attributes.name: Haz38 - Risk Prioritization - Future Conditions in Prioritization
attributes.proposal: Are future climate conditions incorporated into prioritization decisions?

attributes.name: Haz39 - Review of Inputs and Assumptions - Input Data Quality Review
attributes.proposal: Does the plan critically evaluate the quality and completeness of its input datasets?

attributes.name: Haz40 - Review of Inputs and Assumptions - Data Gaps
attributes.proposal: Does the plan identify important data gaps?

attributes.name: Haz41 - Review of Inputs and Assumptions - Expert and Stakeholder Inputs
attributes.proposal: Are expert judgments and stakeholder inputs documented?

attributes.name: Haz42 - Review of Inputs and Assumptions - Local Knowledge
attributes.proposal: Does the plan explain how local knowledge influenced hazard identification and risk assessment?

attributes.name: Haz43 - Review of Inputs and Assumptions - Municipal and Utility Consultation
attributes.proposal: Were municipal departments, utility providers, public health agencies, and emergency managers consulted when identifying hazards and assets?

attributes.name: Haz44 - Review of Inputs and Assumptions - Data and Assessment Updates
attributes.proposal: Does the plan include a process for updating datasets and revising risk assessments as better information becomes available?

attributes.name: Haz45 - Overall Assessment - Missing Hazards
attributes.proposal: Based on available evidence, are any significant hazards missing from the assessment?

attributes.name: Haz46 - Overall Assessment - Missing Critical Assets
attributes.proposal: Based on available evidence, are any critical community assets missing from the assessment?

attributes.name: Haz47 - Overall Assessment - Opportunities to Improve Accuracy
attributes.proposal: Are there opportunities to improve the accuracy of risk estimates through better datasets, updated modeling, or additional local analysis?

attributes.name: Haz48 - Overall Assessment - Decision-Usefulness
attributes.proposal: Does the risk assessment appear sufficient to support prioritization of mitigation actions and funding decisions?

attributes.name: Haz49 - Advocate Lens - Hazard and Social Vulnerability Overlap
attributes.proposal: Does the plan identify where vulnerable populations and high-risk physical hazards overlap?

attributes.name: Haz50 - Advocate Lens - Equitable Investment Prioritization
attributes.proposal: Does the plan prioritize mitigation investments in areas facing both high hazard exposure and high social vulnerability?

attributes.name: Haz51 - Advocate Lens - Historically Underserved Neighborhoods
attributes.proposal: Does the plan evaluate whether historically underserved neighborhoods have received proportional attention in the risk assessment?

attributes.name: Haz52 - Advocate Lens - Community Assets and Social Infrastructure
attributes.proposal: Does the plan recognize community assets and social networks as resilience resources, not just physical infrastructure?

attributes.name: Haz53 - Advocate Lens - Community-Generated Data
attributes.proposal: Does the plan incorporate local, community-generated, or resident-collected data where available?
